subject: Data controls & custom retention - Carelytics discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Zhou <emma.zhou@carelytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Data controls & custom retention - Carelytics discovery follow-up

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next-step plan so we can keep momentum. I pulled out the items you emphasized around data handling and compliance:

- PII classification: Carelytics will treat user identifiers and clinical notes as PII and needs strong minimization controls.
- Retention preference: default 0-retention for transcripts where possible; for analytics payloads you asked about a 14-day window, with an option for 7-day in pilot.
- Audit & evidence: SOC 2 report and API access logs for audits; you may need access to hashed request logs for investigations.
- Residency: US-only region is required for the pilot.

What we propose now (minimal, achievable pilot):
1) Pilot with 7-day token-level logs for a subset of endpoints (non-identifiable analytics)
2) 0-retention toggle for direct transcript capture endpoints (redwood-managed)
3) Exchange of SOC 2 summary and KMS integration notes by Monday (attached)
4) Mutual action plan: agree on data flows and sign an addendum for the pilot by 11/20

Can Marissa and Karthik join a 30-min technical sync next week to scope the mechanics (Karthik can speak to KMS and log redaction options)?

Next steps for Carelytics: please confirm whether 7-day for analytics + 0-retention for transcripts is acceptable as a starting point, and whether you want us to scope a separate 14-day/analytics option for later.

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson

From: Emma Zhou <emma.zhou@carelytics.com>

Subject: Re: Data controls & custom retention - Carelytics discovery follow-up

Thanks Avery — good summary. A few clarifications from my side:

- We can accept 7-day logs for analytics as a pilot, but transcripts that include PHI must be 0-retention or kept only within our VPC (we will confirm which endpoints contain PHI).
- For audit evidence, we require: SOC 2 Type II summary, list of available API logs (fields + TTL), and proof of KMS integration for customer keys. Your attachments helped.
- Residency: must be US-only for production. Pilot can run in a restricted us-west region.

Can you have your security/infra engineer call me Monday afternoon to walk through the log fields and how redaction/hashed IDs work? I’m copying our security mailbox for visibility.

Emma Zhou
Head of Product Security | Carelytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Zhou <emma.zhou@carelytics.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data controls & custom retention - Carelytics discovery follow-up

Emma — thanks for the clear ask. I’m Redwood’s solutions engineer (infra/security) — quick technical notes to address the items you listed and the proposed pilot: 

1) Retention mechanics
   - We support per-endpoint TTLs at the routing layer. For the pilot we can set transcripts=0 (no persistent storage) and analytics=7d. The proposed-retention-schedule-carelytics.csv in the thread maps endpoints to TTLs; we can edit after the sync.

2) PII / PHI handling
   - We offer request-time redaction hooks (customer-supplied rules) and post-ingest hashed-id substitution. Both are configurable per-tenant and can be toggled without code deployments.

3) Logs & audit evidence
   - Attach: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (high-level), and a short KMS integration note (kms-integration-note.txt).
   - For audits we can provide API call metadata (timestamp, route, model version, truncated request hash) for the 7-day analytics window. Full request payloads for transcripts set to 0 are not stored.

4) KMS / keys
   - We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM (bring-your-own). Integration requires a single IAM role and an initial key rotation configuration. See kms-integration-note.txt for the steps.

5) Residency
   - We can pin pilot traffic to us-west-2 and restrict routing to US-regions only for the account.

Proposed next actions:
- Technical sync: Tue 11/17 10:00am PT (30m). Action: Karthik to demo TTL toggle and redaction rules.
- After sync: deliver an updated retention CSV and a short addendum for the pilot (Avery + Marissa).
- Timeline: pilot kickoff target 11/30 if addendum signed by 11/20.

If that aligns I’ll prepare a one-page tech note to include in the addendum.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Infra & Security | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
